title: An umbrella review of the benefits and risks associated with youths' interactions with electronic screens
authors: Sanders, T.; Noetel, M.; Parker, P.; Del Pozo Cruz, B.; Biddle, S.; Ronto, R.; Hulteen, R.; Parker, R.; Thomas, G.; De Cocker, K.; Salmon, J.; Hesketh, K.; Weeks, N.; Arnott, H.; Devine, E.; Vasconcellos, R.; Pagano, R.; Sherson, J.; Conigrave, J.; Lonsdale, C.
paper_type: Umbrella review / overview of reviews (meta-analysis of meta-analyses)
engine: anomalyco/opencode (ReproAI) — DeepSeek V4 Flash via uniGPT
audit_mode: static audit + independent reimplementation (R metafor; Python DL-on-z cross-check)

provenance.input_source: Study-level primary data in Studies.csv; effect/review/quality tables

pipeline.manuscript: reports/manuscript.Rmd (papaja) with dynamic inline numbers via make_manuscript_info.R

reimplementation.language_r: R 4.6.1, metafor 5.0-1 (mirrors authors' run_metaanalysis: rma measure=COR, mean-imputed N)
reimplementation.language_python: Python 3.8.10 — independent DerSimonian-Laird on Fisher-z for 8 headline effects
reimplementation.headline_result: 18/18 paper-quoted pooled effects (r, 95% CI, k, N, p) reproduced to the paper's 2-dp precision
reimplementation.sensitivity: Shared Studies.csv uses sentinel -999/''/#N/A converted to NA (authors' read_sheet na=c('-999','','#N/A')); must be replicated before mean N imputation.

summary: Primary quantitative synthesis fully reproducible from shared study-level data via the shared targets pipeline; every pooled effect verified independently. Remaining findings are traceability/documentation nuances around the risk-of-bias and aggregate-sample tallies (102-review Table-1 subset vs the 217-row raw QA file) and minor prose/code hygiene.
